title: Pinned-model canary framework: configurable traffic splits, gating metrics, and performance-profile publish
creator: Aisha Verma
description: Enable customers and internal SREs to run canary and A/B experiments for new model versions that are behind customer pins. The feature will let users declare a pinned model family (e.g., gpt-redwood-2/sha:abc123) and create an ephemeral canary variant that receives a controllable fraction of traffic. The platform should collect and evaluate performance profiles (latency, token cost, top-line quality signal from eval hooks) and optionally publish a verified performance profile if the canary passes gates. We need UI, API, rollout orchestration, and automatic rollback/publish behavior tied to observable gates and audit logs.
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /pins/{pin_id}/canaries creates a canary variant with fields: model_version, initial_split_percent, gate_config, expiration
Traffic control: Can set traffic split down to 0.1% and schedule gradual ramp-up steps (e.g., 1% -> 5% -> 20%)
Gating: Support gating on latency p95, error rate, and a custom quality metric returned by eval hooks; gates can be set with thresholds and evaluation windows
Performance profile publish: Option to auto-publish the canary's performance profile to the pinned variant only if gates pass for a configured window
Rollbacks: Automatic rollback to baseline and alerting on gate failure; audit log entry for publish/rollback actions
Console: Console view for the pin showing canary timeline, split history, gate evaluations, and raw metric feeds
Permissions: Only users with pin-edit permission can create/confirm canaries; audit entries record actor and reason
Observability: Per-canary tracing and aggregated token/cost breakdown stored for minimum 30 days (configurable as enterprise add-on)
updates: 2026-03-10: PRD drafted, scoped MVP to support three gate types (latency, error_rate, eval_score). Linked design doc and infra spike notes.

2026-03-11: Eng spike complete: found two approach options for traffic splitting (proxy-based vs runtime routing). Proxy-based needs fewer runtime changes but adds routing hotpath; runtime routing requires KV cache awareness. Decision leaning toward runtime routing with guards for initial MVP.
2026-03-12: Security asked for audit schema; added requirement to include model sha, canary id, actor, and gate snapshot. Marked security_review_required.
2026-03-13: Tech spec draft posted in Confluence. Frontend wireframes attached. Backend owners assigned: runtime routing (ENG-2741), metrics pipeline changes (ENG-2810).
Next: Coord with Console team for UI and UX review (design review scheduled 2026-03-16).
notes: Trade-offs discussed: strict runtime routing preserves KV cache locality but increases complexity for dedicated deployments. Proxy-based approach easier to rollout for Hosted, but requires additional hop costing latency. We will prototype runtime routing for Private/Dedicated and keep proxy approach as fallthrough for Hosted if runtime feature flag disabled.
implementation_plan: MVP: API + runtime routing + simple gate evaluator + console canary card
Phase 2: More gate types (distribution shifts), automatic bias/quality regression detection, canary A/B experiment templates
Phase 3: Cross-pin experiments for dataset-level comparisons and cohort-targeted rollouts
